analysis:
This PR changes only scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py, an offline CI test script. It does not touch provider runtime, the coordinator wire contract, key custody, attestation, or the prefix cache code that T-041 covers, so no production trust boundary changes.

What the head side shows (lines 152-187): the test's VALIDATE_GIT constant now expects a hardened step that validates a restored .git cache. The step discards .git if it is a symlink or not a directory, or if it contains symlinks, non-sample hooks, or a config setting core.fsmonitor, core.hooksPath, or include/includeIf. It still runs git fsck. This tightens CI against a poisoned cache from a prior run. The test runs the real script against healthy, blobless, damaged and empty clones (head 1089-1118 per the ranges; base lines 1021-1052). This is a CI supply-chain improvement and no regression.

Also added: a CACHE_GATE step (CI_ACTIONS_CACHE=off) so Darkbloom Sandbox runners without a Darkbloom cache skip GitHub Actions cache steps (head 176-196). Tests still pin SAVE_CACHES to push events on master/dev and pin persist-credentials: false on checkouts (base 927-1019). I verified neither weakens those pins.

Open question: the patch excerpt is truncated. Head lines 468-1407 were not supplied, so I could not check whether any assertion was loosened elsewhere. The actual workflow YAML and composite action were not in this batch, so I cannot confirm they match the test's expectations. The new git-cache hardening depends on them. I record this as an unverified integration contract rather than a finding. A reviewer of the workflow files should confirm the cache gate and the git validation step are applied to every cache step and every checkout.
